name: ansible-flow-designer
description: Visual, top-down designer for Ansible automation flows: sketch typed nodes and ports, run a walking skeleton, then bind nodes to modules, roles and playbooks.

afd.codegen.onSave.markdownDescription: Write generated code to `generated/` next to the flow whenever a flow without errors is saved. Files edited by hand are never overwritten without asking.

afd.environment.kind.markdownDescription: Where Ansible runs. `auto`: a container when an image is set (here or in the Red Hat Ansible extension's execution environment settings), else a local interpreter (VS Code Remote, venv). Native Windows needs a container.

afd.environment.image.markdownDescription: Execution environment image for the probe and runs, e.g. `registry.example.net/ee/netops:2.19`. Empty: use `ansible.executionEnvironment.image` when the Red Hat Ansible extension enables execution environments.

afd.environment.containerEngine.description: Container engine for the image (auto: the Red Hat Ansible setting, else docker).

afd.environment.containerOptions.markdownDescription: Extra `docker run` / `podman run` arguments, one per item (e.g. `-v`, `~/.ssh:/home/ansible/.ssh:ro` for keys).

afd.environment.python.markdownDescription: Python with ansible-core 2.19+ for local mode. Empty: `ansible.python.interpreterPath`, else `python3`.

afd.run.inventory.markdownDescription: Inventory for runs, relative to the repository root. Empty: the default from `ansible.cfg`.

afd.run.askVaultPassword.markdownDescription: Ask for the vault password before a run (`auto`: when the inventory or repository vars contain vault data). The password is used for that run only and never stored.

afd.awx.url.markdownDescription: AWX address for _Launch in AWX_, e.g. `https://awx.example.net`. The token is kept in VS Code's secret storage (_Set AWX Token_), never in settings.

afd.awx.verifyTls.markdownDescription: Verify AWX's TLS certificate. Turn off only for a lab AWX with a self-signed certificate.

languageModelTools.name: afd_flow_edit
languageModelTools.userDescription: Edit an Ansible flow with ops that name nodes by key (never IDs). The ops run in order, all or nothing; nodes added earlier in the batch can be used by later ops. Returns what changed, new problems and the new revision.
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Edit an Ansible flow with ops that name nodes by key (never IDs). The ops run in order, all or nothing; nodes added earlier in the batch can be used by later ops. Returns what changed, new problems and the new revision. Ansible Flow Designer flows (*.flow.yaml); see the ansible-flow skill.

path.description: The flow file (*.flow.yaml), relative to the workspace root. Default: the flow open in the designer, or the only flow.

ops.description: Ops in order; flow_reference topic ops lists them with examples.

anyOf.description: Add a node. after continues from an output port: a free port is wired to the new node, a wired one gets the node on its wire (so a chain grows: a new flow is start -> done). on_wire does the same for a wired port only, failed_to wires its failed_hosts. The key comes from the title unless given. Use in to add it inside a subflow.

type.description: start (one, on the top level; hosts enter), end (hosts leave; outcome success or failed), task, subflow (has an inner level), decision (true/false per host), approval (a person approves), parallel (branches), join (branches meet).

title.description: Human name shown on the canvas.

key.description: Key of the new node; default: from the title. Must be new on its level.

in.description: Subflow whose inner level gets the node (default: top).

after.description: Continue from this output port: wired to the new node, or the node goes on its wire when the port is wired already.

on_wire.description: Put the new node on the wire leaving this output port (between both ends).

failed_to.description: Wire the new node's failed_hosts to this node.

intent.description: What the node should do, in a sentence. Skeleton runs print it.

items.description: A port name. Which ports a node has depends on its type: see the port catalog. Parallel branch ports are branch_1, branch_2, ...

ports.description: Optional ports enabled beyond the type defaults (e.g. unreachable, timeout, always on a task).

handler.description: Marks a failure handler node (what kind of handling it does)

condition.description: Decision nodes: Jinja expression evaluated per host.

branches.description: Parallel nodes: number of branch ports branch_1..branch_n (default 2)

join_mode.description: Join nodes: per host, all = every branch delivered the host (default), any = at least one

type.description: Value type. host_list is a list of inventory hosts or groups.

default.description: Inputs: value used when none is given.

from.description: Where the value comes from: <node_key>.<output> (an earlier node's output), flow.<input> (a flow input), or impl.register[.path] (outputs: the bound task's registered result).

targets.description: Flow inputs only: this host_list input seeds the start node's host set.

inputs.description: Values the node needs, usually from: an earlier node or a flow input.

languageModelTools.name: afd_flow_new
languageModelTools.userDescription: Create a new Ansible flow diagram: a *.flow.yaml file that Ansible Flow Designer draws and turns into playbooks. Use it whenever the user asks for an Ansible flow, flow diagram or automation flow, instead of drawing one in PlantUML, Mermaid or draw.io. The flow starts as start -> done with a devices host_list input; then add steps with flow_edit (add_node after start.ok_hosts puts the first step between them).
languageModelTools.modelDescription: Create a new Ansible flow diagram: a *.flow.yaml file that Ansible Flow Designer draws and turns into playbooks. Use it whenever the user asks for an Ansible flow, flow diagram or automation flow, instead of drawing one in PlantUML, Mermaid or draw.io. The flow starts as start -> done with a devices host_list input; then add steps with flow_edit (add_node after start.ok_hosts puts the first step between them). Ansible Flow Designer flows (*.flow.yaml); see the ansible-flow skill.
